Prevention: Plant pest-free seedlings from certified sources.
Use clean, pest-free organic mulch after transplanting.
Destroy all host crops ( Tagetes , amaranthus, old potato crop etc) and debris before planting.
Use a shade net (size 400 µm) / tunnel for 3-5 weeks while in nursery to prevent attack by white flies.
Conserve natural enemies (lace wing larvae, bugs) by leaving a natural hedge of flowering plants.
Plant repellent crops such as coriander or
Mexican marigold after 3-4 rows of tomato to repel the white flies.
Plant trap crops like beans, maize among others around the field.
Avoid high doses of nitrogen fertiliser, which can make the plants more attractive to sucking pests
Monitoring: Monitor with yellow sticky traps (at least one or two per acre) to check for general presence of the pest.
Look for whitish adults on the underside of young leaves.
Look for small white insects that fly when the plant is shaken.
Consider direct control when 3 adult white flies are present per leaf.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide always wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
Follow the instructions on the product label on dosage, maximum applications, PHI,Re
entry interval, disposal of pesticide waste amongst others.
Use list of registered pesticides (PCPB): www.pcpb.go.ke
